articles.title: FAA issues national ground stop – lifted 4.5 hours later

top_comments: For those interested, there was a 2009 outage of the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure that at a surface level seems like it could be a similar failure mode. At the very least, it is an interesting read on how the FAAs systems operate, since a lot of the discussion so far has been wild speculation from people with little knowledge on how the national airspace system actually operates: https://www.oig.dot.gov/library-item/29670Of particular note is this section: Risks of FTI Outages for Existing Operational Services As of December 2009, Harris reported that there are a total of 20,982 services operating on the FTI network. While FAA has transitioned all 1,808 IP services supporting FAA flight plans to the new FTI fiber optic network, additional risks will be introduced when the Agency begins transitioning other FAA services, such as En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) and NextGen platforms, which also require IP technology to operate. Moreover, there are 19,174 existing services that may be transitioned to the new FTI fiber optic network. According to FAA, transitioning these remaining services is important because FTI now connects older FAA systems that provide safety-critical voice and surveillance radar information by utilizing Time Division Multiplex (TDM) technology, instead of IP services.

starting to see some explanations for what's going onhttps://www.wsj.com/us-news/faa-temporarily-halts-flights-ac...> The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn’t immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-issues-nationwide-ground-st...> An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News. The system is operated by L3Harris, which did not immediately respond to CBS News' request for comment.

Info on this is amazingly sparse. Apparently Sec. Duffy posted something on X/Twitter, and that's all the news media have.Looking at LAX departures, it looks like nothing has departed since about 10:30 AM PST, and everything later is showing Delayed or Cancelled. There are times after Delayed, but it's not clear those times mean anything. Some are now in the past."flysfo.com" is too overloaded to display departures. Stuck at "loading...".JFK departure status shows almost solid "Delayed".No good explanations anywhere.

articles.title: Nvidia Allegedly Engineered Scarcity by Funding AI Startups to Buy Its GPUs
articles.summary: Nvidia Allegedly Engineered Scarcity by Funding AI Startups to Buy Its GPUs

top_comments: 40 year old gamer here having a flashback of all anti- competition practices Nvidia sustained for decades. Who here remembers GameWorks and PhysX effectively sabotaging multi-vendor optimization in titles like Witcher 3 and Watch Dogs? Expensive Gsync monitors? Trying to force OEMs to be GeForce partners in exchange for full GPU support? Forcing EVGA exit from the market? And then completely shafting gamers when crypto and AI markets opened up?
I thought we knew a year ago that nVidia was doing circular finance?https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/dec/28/nvidia-in...

Nvidia wants to ensure data center companies that are optimized for AI like Nebius stock their buildings with Nvidia chips instead of AMD or ASICs so of course it is smart business sense to partner with them or take stakes in them.Nvidia gives Nebius first access to their newest chips, ensures they get deployed at top performance, allows Nvidia to recognize the revenue upfront, and ends up owning equity in the upside.Nebius gets the best chips first, gets cheaper financing due to the obvious security granted by having one of the most valuable companies in the world standing behind them, etc.It sounds like a mutually beneficial deal rather than something shady to me.By the way they report demand is 10x supply so I think everyone in here hoping for some cheap GPUs soon is kidding themselves. Eventually RAM might get cheaper because it's easier to build new factories to produce commoditized RAM but TSMC is the bottleneck for advanced chips and it isn't resolving anytime in the foreseeable future.I'm buying the dip from this silliness.

articles.title: Live airband on all frequencies from KORS. Victoria, CA also ground stopped
articles.summary: Live airband on all frequencies from KORS. Victoria, CA also ground stopped

top_comments: Hi all. Thanks for the interest. I'm going to post an impromptu blog post here just explaining what this is. The rather unfortunate ground stop today made this unexpectedly useful with the pilots here on Orcas just to get a sense of the chatter in our airspace re the situation.This is an ETTUS B210 attached to a dual 4090 box. It's a polyphase channelizer that takes the entire airband, channelizes it using cuda code on GPU, demodulates it, detects transmissions, throws away data tx and then feeds the tx through a voice model I created for transcription. A separate LLM reads the transcriptions to create a situational awareness picture of the airspace.I'm interested in open sourcing this and making it available for folks who can run an ETTUS B210 or high quality SDR with enoguh bandwidth and a local GPU machine, so that we can cover more airpsace.This was born out of an incident we had not too long ago where a pilot around KORS (based at Friday Harbor) lost the engine in his 172, and put it in the water in front of a ferry and was picked up by the ferry. We're a pretty close bunch on Orcas Island and we only heard about it days later via social media. That felt completely unacceptable, and I set out to create a radio that could monitor everything in real-time, all the time, and alert on emergencies. That has extended to transcribing and creating situational awareness for a chunk of airspace.I'm an IFR pilot. I fly a T206H regularly in IMC around here and I'm a ground instructor. You can email me at mark@defiant.com or find me on x at mmaunder if you'd like to connect. I'm particularly interested in hearing from folks who can run a station on their own hardware and are under bravo or a charlie or even just somewhere interesting re airspace.

These are raw transcripts unedited by me that I extracted possibly related to the groundstop, generated at time of posting: 2143Z, 126.400 Victoria Ground (weak signal): "Yeah, we just uh communication issues, so we got the traffic stopped on [unintelligible]" 2151Z, 134.800 Vancouver Centre, pilot of a flight ending "364": "We're saying they just have an alternate plan. They've been getting lower and lower 48 right now. We're on the phone with you, they are saying cannot show any reason why we would be out of communication to Seattle. So just otherwise we do have some alternates that we're talking about, but we just want to see, you see anything on your end that we cannot proceed to Seattle?" 2152Z, 134.800 Vancouver Centre, same pilot: "Okay, sounds good. Yeah, we appreciate that. We'll be staying by and we'll just kind of get the alternate plans for ready to go. Thank you." 2159Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Seacraft 304, just a heads up here, there is a ground stop for an aircraft about into Vancouver at this time. I'm sure you have a VFR slot, seeing where you're headed there now, so I'd like to be still going to take you, but it just has stopped that you might end up getting turned around." 2159Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Sorry, that's all inbound aircraft, ground stop." 2200Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Yeah, it's not affecting anything airborne at this time. We're just about departing anything for Vancouver and Calgary at this time." 2201Z, 126.400 Victoria Ground, pilot (weak signal): "Hey Ground, it's Jazz 270, and I'm guessing there's a flow for Vancouver." 2203Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, pilot: "Uh just wanted to confirm uh there's a ground stop uh going into Vancouver on this frequency?" 2203Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Encore 3325, that's correct. Nothing is departing to land at Vancouver at this time." 2204Z, 134.800 Vancouver Centre, pilot: "Yeah, right now they said normal ops continue, but we'll see what happens once we get closer." 2217Z, 126.125 Vancouver Departure, pilot: "Yeah, you guys not having any of the issues that they're having in the US right now?" 2217Z, 126.125 Vancouver Departure: "Uh, apparently the ones uh seeing ground stop for the 14 major airports I've just got a few minutes. Okay, thanks." 2227Z, 126.400 Victoria Ground, pilot: "Encore 58, information Papa, requesting flow through to Vancouver for 2255." Reply: "Roger, 2255 on the flight plan."

If you scroll back to 2:03pm (the time this link was posted) there was this interaction:14:03:04 Uh just wanted to confirm uh there's a ground stop uh going into Vancouver on this frequency?14:03:10 Encore 3325, that's correct. Nothing is departing to land at Vancouver at this time.

articles.title: Terminal borders that don't cost a cell
articles.summary: Terminal borders that don't cost a cell

top_comments: A much better alternative to this would be to for more terminal emulators to implement overstrike mode (DECSET 20, as available on the VK100). That way you could just draw border characters over existing text cells to achieve the same thing.Unfortunately mintty is the only terminal emulator I'm aware of which supports overstrike [0], as this would open up a world of new possibilities for TUI apps if more widely supported.[0] https://github.com/mintty/mintty/wiki/CtrlSeqs#overstrike

I love this work and everything else Ratatui does but I have to ask: if you're changing the terminal protocol and the terminal itself to do this, why not do something more ambitious; a full monospaced information-dense UI framework, a terminal designed for user interfaces, rather than one designed to replicate the limitations of dumb terminals?

This is pretty cool but this does feel like we are just reinventing another GUI display at this point.I don't generally like TUI's and think one gets more flexibility with raw text interfaces and being able to glue things together is more important then them looking nice. I think less fancy out put is better to be honest.

articles.summary: Found: A protein that drives ageing without unleashing inflammation

top_comments: Paper: https://www.cell.com/immunity/fulltext/S1074-7613(26)00440-1Granzyme K is the protein.

From the abstract of the paper, significantly more nuance.> Despite persistent immune aging phenotypes, GzmK deficiency markedly attenuated organ aging, effectively uncoupling immune and tissue aging... These findings identify GzmK as a tissue-specific driver of organismal aging but not immune aging or systemic inflammaging.
Paywall

What is really impressive about this project and llama.cpp as well is that they keep finding new ways to speed up the code on the same hardware. Every time I upgrade (once a month or so) there is usually a 5 to 10% speed boost.edit: Just to verify: I had planned to upgrade today, ran my usual benchmark prior and after and the runtime went from 4:22 to 3:59. That's a really long prompt (50K tokens) so prefill is a good chunk of that and the rest is spent on token generation.

Awesome! ggml and llama.cpp are the Linux of the AI world. Driving local inference one bit at a time.Wishing you unlimited power and may you never see a day of low battery. Respect and Love. Keep it up.
Long time llama.cpp user (and user of other ggml based AI programs) running on my crappy AMD card that only supports vulkan and it's usable thanks to GGML and llama.cpp, great program great project.
